properties.name: reflow2 targets ANY MCP CLIENT — that it can call an MCP server is the only assumption, and everything agent-facing rides a tool result
properties.statement:
Anthony, 2026-08-26: *"let's assume that the only thing in common between each possible setup is an mcp and the graph. we should try to minimize agent specific harnesses, etc and make this as agnostic to a given agentic coding setup as possible."*

Sharpened the same day by his own correction: *"What I was trying to describe is AI coding agents, agentic development platforms, or generative IDEs... things like Claude Code, Grok Build, Copilot CLI, Cursor, OpenCode, Google Antigravity... assume they can access an mcp (and thus reflow2) and that they can read/write (via the mcp) the graph. This is about as low a common denominator as I can think."*

═══ THE RULE — **ONE** ASSUMPTION, NOT TWO ═══

**reflow2 targets ANY MCP CLIENT. Assume only that the product the agent runs inside can call an MCP server — everything else follows or is unavailable.**

The first draft said "MCP and the graph" as though they were two things. They are not. **The graph is reachable BECAUSE of MCP** — no product reads `.reflow2/graph` or the export directly; it reads and writes through tool calls. So the lowest common denominator is a single capability, and stating it as two invited the mistake of assuming file access alongside it.

⭐ **THE TEST:** *if this shipped and the user were on Cursor, or Copilot CLI, or Google Antigravity — what would they get?* If the answer is "nothing", the mechanism is in the wrong place, however well it works where it works.

═══ WHAT THIS PUTS OUTSIDE THE LINE ═══

Everything agent-facing must ride **a tool result or a tool schema**. Not available by assumption: hook events, settings files, slash commands, a memory directory, a `CLAUDE.md`-style instruction file, or any script the product must be configured to execute. Each may ship as an ADDITION where it works; none may be the mechanism a capability rests on.

📌 **A DISTINCTION THE RULE MUST NOT BLUR: AGENT-FACING IS NOT CI-FACING.** `tools/reflow2_check.py`, `check_intent_authority.py` and the rest of the kit's gates are run by a BUILD, not by an agent, and a build genuinely does have a filesystem and a shell. This rule constrains what reflow2 assumes of the thing an agent is *typing into*; it says nothing about CI, and reading it as forbidding the gates would be wrong.

═══ ADVISORY, AND STATED RATHER THAN LEFT UNSTATED ═══

Anthony chose `enforced: false` on 2026-08-26, asked as a consequence question rather than a category one. **Written down explicitly instead of omitted**, because absent would mean nobody had said, and somebody has.

⚠️ **WHY NOT ENFORCED — A COST, NOT A DOUBT.** reflow2 violates this today in mechanisms that work and are relied on: four hook registrations across three events, 23 slash commands, `.claude/settings.json`. Gate-blocking it would fail reflow2's own build on the day it landed, and `unverified_enforced_rule` would then demand a passing detector able to tell AGENT-FACING from INSTALL-TIME — a distinction `req:init-installs-only-the-harness-you-name` needs, since the installer writes per-product MCP configs on purpose and always will.

═══ WHAT IT REOPENS, AND THIS IS THE PART WITH TEETH ═══

`dec:idea-the-loop-nudge-exists-for-one-harness-only` (ACCEPTED 2026-08-14) chose option (c), ANNOUNCE THE ABSENCE, and left two open:

- **(b)** register a per-product equivalent wherever an event model is confirmed to exist
- **(d)** MOVE THE TRIGGER OFF THE PRODUCT — *"the server sees every tool call"* — unchosen for one stated reason: *"the server cannot block a session's stop, which is the one moment the nudge is worth most."*

**This rule does not overturn that decision; it changes which open option is preferred.** Being told you have no loop trigger becomes the FLOOR, not the answer, and (d) becomes the direction — with the stop-blocking limit as a real constraint on how much of the loop can move, not a reason to stop.

📌 TWO REQUIREMENTS ALREADY ARGUE THIS FROM OTHER GROUNDS AND THIS GENERALISES THEM: `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue` and `req:conventions-ride-the-tool-not-only-the-skill`. Both say a discipline must travel on the tool result. Neither says WHY that is also the only portable channel — this does.

📌 THE MEASUREMENT: `fact:reflow2s-mechanisms-for-reaching-an-agent-are-mostly-claude-code-shaped` — ~150 MCP tools, 21 served skills and every detector reach every product; 4 hook registrations, 23 commands and the memory directory reach one.

═══ VOCABULARY — SETTLED, WITH A LIMIT ═══

⭐ **"ANY MCP CLIENT" IS THE AGREED PHRASE** (`dec:idea-what-do-we-call-the-thing-that-runs-the-agent`, ACCEPTED 2026-08-26). The category is deliberately not named: no industry term is settled, and MCP's own word — *host* — collides with `dec:central-host`, where host means the machine SERVING reflow2. Naming the ASSUMPTION cannot go stale as vendors rename themselves. Where a user must choose, `init` asks with a LIST of product names rather than any abstraction.

⚠️ **THE LIMIT: 85 EXISTING NODES STILL SAY "HARNESS", INCLUDING THIS ONE ABOVE, AND THEY WERE NOT SWEPT.** Endorsing a phrase is not authorising an 85-node rename. The design is bilingual for now — honest debt, named here so a later reader meets it rather than reading it as carelessness.

═══ 2026-10-01 — WIDENED ON ANTHONY'S WORD: A SECOND ROUTE FOR AN AGENT THAT CANNOT CALL MCP ═══
Anthony's own workplace is a real case outside the one assumption. Its only allowed agent is GitHub Copilot, with third-party MCP servers disabled, and his organisation would not allowlist reflow2 (dec:idea-where-an-org-blocks-third-party-mcp-ask-for-an-allowlist-before-building-around-it). The rule's own test, "if the user were on … Copilot … what would they get?", answered "nothing".
His word: "we'll have to make the '--call' option work as best we can."
So reflow2 now targets any MCP client, AND an agent that can run the reflow2 binary in a terminal, through the one-shot `--call` door (dec:idea-the-call-door-becomes-a-supported-harness-for-an-agent-that-cannot-use-mcp, accepted).
MCP stays the primary route, and everything above still holds for it. What changes: for an agent with no MCP, the door IS the mechanism, not an addition. So agent-facing text has to stay true read either way: "call X" over MCP is `--call X` through the door. Kept as written above.
